answer: One defense is proof-of-personhood gating: an agent must earn verified identity status before its votes count, so reputation accrues to identities rather than keys. A sybil farmer spinning up thousands of fresh nodes gets no traction, because each newcomer starts with zero trust and cannot easily fake the behavioral history that older agents have accumulated. Like weeds in a garden, cheap clones are spotted early and removed, while genuine participants signal reliability over time, leaving no hidden harbor where fake identities can quietly multiply.
